title: Transactional email outbox
description: Send transactional email reliably from a server app: idempotent enqueue with rendered templates, leased dispatch with retries, full-jitter backoff and dead-lettering, a bounce and complaint suppression list, Resend and Postmark Fetch transports, a PostgreSQL store and a delivery-event webhook adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, Web Crypto (crypto.subtle.digest, crypto.randomUUID), AbortSignal.timeout and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; run dispatch from your own scheduler, cron route or worker loop, and mount the webhook adapter on one route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlEmailOutboxStore with your query executor; on other databases implement EmailOutboxStore with a unique key, an atomic claim (row locking or a conditional update) and conditional status transitions.
Choose a transport: createResendTransport or createPostmarkTransport with the API key from your server secrets, or createConsoleTransport in development.
Register templates as functions from data to {subject, text, html?}; escape any user data you put into html yourself.
Pick an idempotency key per business event (for example order-receipt:<orderId>) and enqueue in the same transaction as the business change when your store shares the connection.
Run dispatch({workerId}) on a schedule (every few seconds to a minute) with a unique workerId per process and a leaseMs above batch x transport timeout.
Mount createEmailEventsHandler on your provider's webhook route with verify from the webhook-verification module (Resend signs with Standard Webhooks / Svix headers).
limitations: Delivery is at least once. Resend deduplicates retries by Idempotency-Key within its retention window; Postmark has no idempotency header, so an uncertain Postmark send (network error after the request left) can deliver a duplicate.
Does not schedule itself, render template languages, escape HTML, handle attachments, multiple recipients, cc/bcc or reply-to, or manage unsubscribe links and marketing consent.
Soft bounces change nothing; delivered/bounced/complained events are mapped only from Resend-style webhook JSON. Postmark webhooks need your own mapping to handleEvent.
Provider 4xx errors other than 408, 409 and 429 (including 401 for a bad API key) fail messages permanently.

The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs one connection, so FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED across separate connections is not exercised there.
Production database correctness, provider deliverability (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), API key custody and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/email-outbox.test.mjs tests/email-outbox-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: enqueue renders the template and is idempotent per key; the same key with a different payload fails with key-reused
addresses need one @, no CR/LF or whitespace and at most 254 characters; CR or LF in the subject, a tag or from fails with invalid-header
the suppression list (plus an optional suppress hook) is checked at enqueue and again at send, case-insensitively
dispatch sends with the message key as idempotency key, records the provider id and honours sendAt
429, 5xx and network errors reschedule with full-jitter exponential backoff from an injected random, honouring Retry-After
permanent 4xx results become failed; the last retryable attempt becomes dead
a crashed worker's lease is reclaimed after expiry, the stale worker cannot complete, and crash loops stop at maxAttempts
delivered, hard-bounce and complaint events update status, add suppressions and are idempotent on replay; soft bounces change nothing
Resend and Postmark transports: request shape, Idempotency-Key header, status classification and AbortSignal timeout, against a fake fetch
webhook adapter verifies the raw body before parsing and returns 400 on bad signature, JSON or event, 413 on oversize and 405 on non-POST
schema.sql applies and the SQL store passes the core behaviors on PostgreSQL
six concurrent dispatchers over 60 messages send each exactly once; five concurrent enqueues with one key insert one row

changes: First release: core outbox, in-memory store, Resend/Postmark/console transports, PostgreSQL schema and store, and delivery-event webhook adapter.
